questions.question_text: In the Azure portal, which navigation path do you use to create a new Microsoft Entra user?

options.label: A
options.text: Azure Active Directory > Users > New user

questions.explanation: According to Microsoft Entra ID documentation, you navigate to Azure Active Directory > Users > New user in the Azure portal to create a user.

questions.question_text: You need to assign a Microsoft 365 license to a security group so that all current and future members can use the service. Which action should you take?

options.label: A
options.text: Assign the license to the group from the Licenses blade in Microsoft Entra ID

options.label: B
options.text: Assign the license to each user individually

options.label: C
options.text: Use Azure AD B2B to assign the license to the group

options.label: D
options.text: Enable Azure AD Connect sync to propagate the license

questions.explanation: Documentation states that licenses can be assigned to groups from the Licenses blade, enabling centralized management.

questions.question_text: A partner organization requires temporary access to an Azure resource. What is the correct step to invite the partner as an external user?

options.label: A
options.text: Invite the partner as a guest user via Azure AD > New user > User type: Guest

options.label: B
options.text: Create a new Azure AD tenant for the partner and invite them

options.label: C
options.text: Sync the partner’s on‑premises accounts using Azure AD Connect

options.label: D
options.text: Assign the partner a built‑in Administrator role in Azure RBAC

questions.explanation: The Azure AD B2B collaboration feature allows you to invite external users as guests, as described in the B2B article.

questions.question_text: An administrator wants to enable self‑service password reset for a specific set of users while keeping the rest of the tenant unchanged. Which configuration approach should be used?

options.label: A
options.text: Enable SSPR at the tenant level and then disable it for specific users via PowerShell

options.label: B
options.text: Configure per‑group SSPR settings in the Azure portal under Authentication methods > Self‑service password reset > Settings

options.label: C
options.text: Enable SSPR for all users and then use conditional access to restrict usage

options.label: D
options.text: Use Azure AD Identity Protection to enforce SSPR

questions.explanation: The Azure portal provides per‑group settings for Self‑service password reset, allowing you to configure the feature for specific groups.

questions.question_text: A user is a member of a Microsoft 365 group that has a license assigned, but the user does not have the license directly assigned to their account. What is the correct behavior?

options.label: A
options.text: The user inherits the license from the group automatically

options.label: B
options.text: The user must be assigned the license individually; group membership does not grant license

options.label: C
options.text: The group must have the "Assign license" permission to propagate the license

options.label: D
options.text: Licenses are assigned at tenant level and are not inherited

questions.explanation: Licenses are not automatically granted to a user based on group membership; they must be assigned directly to the user or through a role assignment.
